name: inprocess-obi-ahb-sha256-zipdma-route-read-f1f6
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU with one real Caliptra sha256_ctrl AHB-Lite target and a ZipDMA in one process.  This declaration asks the DMA master to read the target's own NAME0 register through the target's own AHB-Lite port; the host's routed-DMA admission does not list ahb-lite, so the declaration is refused by name before any model is built.  The file exists as the executable form of that refusal.

evidence.source: third_party/caliptra_upstream_reference/src/sha256/rtl/sha256_params_pkg.sv:24 (SHA256_CORE_NAME0 = 32'h61327368) is the constant the pinned register file returns for NAME0; sha256_reg.sv readback_array[0] selects hwif_in.SHA256_NAME[0].NAME.next on a read, so a read returns the pinned constant

notes: the routed register is NAME0 at 0x00: the profile declares it ro/32-bit and the RTL returns the pinned SHA256_CORE_NAME0 constant, so it is a readable, stable register a fixed read route could capture
the target is mapped at 0x20005000 rather than 0x40000000 because the pinned ZipDMA's SOURCE/DESTINATION CSR fields are 30-bit byte addresses

the refusal this file exercises is the host's routed-DMA admission: dma_transfer.ROUTE_PROTOCOLS and the entry's DMA_ROUTE_PROTOCOLS list apb3/tl-ul/wishbone/axi4-lite and not ahb-lite, so no route plan is produced and no model is built
the F6 route is the only flow this file asks for; its purpose is the named refusal, not a transfer
the AHB-Lite target's own F2/F4/F6 refusal evidence is in runs/p2-ahb-target-20261103/
